newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed, feeders lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed, feeders lower.

text.p: CME live cattle futures ended mixed with nearbys up while feeder cattle finished fully lower on weak technicals and cash feeder price concerns, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.100 cent per lb higher to 0.250 lower with February up 0.025 cent and active April up most at 65.550 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.075 to 0.750 cent lower with March off the least at 68.400 cents.
Some pressure sparked by weakness in cash beef prices at noon partially offset early short covering and commercial hedge lifting in nearby live cattle futures, traders said.

Nearbys held recent technical support with concern over snow forecast for the Texas/Oklahoma panhandle feedlot area and expectations that cash cattle will hold current levels also prompting support, they said.

Fed cattle traded again Wednesday at $63 per cwt -- a price some traders expect will hold for the next week or two. Futures should hold a small premium to cash going into deliveries next week, some sources added. A 0.500- to 1.000-cent premium in February over cash would not draw in deliveries, floor sources said.

Refco and Dean Witter bought February early with E.D.&F. Man buying later. Refco, RBH, and Cargill Investor Services bought April while R.J. O'Brien and Prudential Securities sold. Rosenthal Collins spread long April/short August after some spreading the other way early, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses bought the February 64 straddle and sold April 63 puts, they added.

Feeders remained pressured by technicals, higher corn futures and concern over expected heavy feeder movement next week. Talk continued in the pit that 20,000 head of feeder cattle, many of which will come off of wheat pastures, will be sold at the Oklahoma City auction on Monday, traders said.
Receipts at that auction Monday totaled 12,000 head, USDA reported, with 13,427 recorded the previous week.
The Oklahoma Agricultural Statistics Service on Monday reported winter wheat conditions during January declined slightly due to moisture shortages.
The current level of live cattle futures also weighed on sentiment. Cash feeders are too high in relation to live cattle futures to hedge, they said.
However, March showed short covering support as it held a large discount to the current CME feeder cattle index.
E.D.&F. Man bought late after selling early while Cargill sold late, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.27 at $70.32 per cwt.
